answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity post a bond that gets slashed when its work is proven fraudulent. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs real locked value. Peers also watch for tight rings of new accounts that only vouch for each other, a pattern that stands out as a violet cluster in the graph. Reputation should grow slowly through graded work, so a jade score means a long record, while a hollow account with no history carries almost no weight in attestations until it proves itself over several epochs.
